raw_response:
I only have 1.8 mu, so I cannot spread myself too much. Cotton takes a long season and more picking labor, and in our area wheat-maize is the steadier way to keep grain and cash coming. I have done this for many years, and with such a small piece of land I would keep the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation this year. I watch what neighbors do. If the wheat comes out of winter looking weak, I add a little more fertilizer, but I do not gamble too much because fertilizer and water both cost money. Since I have well water, I will give wheat the important irrigations and then plant maize right after harvest without delaying. That short summer window is always tight, so I keep tillage simple and use what usually works rather than trying anything fancy.
